summary: Six links remains unpromoted after exact transfer, rail continuation, aggregate/modal PFL, analytic modal phase scheduling, Box-FDDP, and tail-search probes. The analytic schedule produced the best generalized approach so far, but the measured blocker remains terminal modal velocity and route energy, not demonstrated rail insufficiency.

transfer_probes.interpretation: wider rail alone does not repair this transfer

count_independent_policy_probes.modal_extension: collective pumping plus energy-gated internal damping and bounded acceleration
count_independent_policy_probes.modal_extension_result: lowered some unwanted motion but did not improve the complete handoff score

analytic_modal_phase_seed.algorithm: regularized minimum-energy finite-horizon controllability-Gramian solve on the exact hanging linear modal model
analytic_modal_phase_seed.result: best generalized six-link upright approach so far, but outside the low-momentum capture envelope

numerical_integrity_boundary.finding: float64 batched tail actions can diverge from the float32 public environment action path at n=6
numerical_integrity_boundary.repair: tail CEM now quantizes candidates to float32 before batch rollout and independently serial-replays its saved result
numerical_integrity_boundary.prior_tail_status: invalid as a replayable controller and excluded from evidence

rail_conclusion: No minimum rail is certified for n=6. Tested failures persisted with large diagnostic headroom, so route/modal phasing is the current blocker.
next_method: deterministic nonlinear continuation of the analytic modal phase seed with explicit cart-travel and terminal-modal-velocity penalties, followed by the same Box-FDDP, serial replay, noisy-gate, and lower-count regression path
